english.title: Arson - recklessly endangering life
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) committed arson in that without lawful excuse

(A)_[destroyed]_
(B)_[damaged]_

by fire **(..SPECIFY PROPERTY..)

(C)_[to the value of **(..SPECIFY VALUE..)]_
(D)_[of a value unknown]_

belonging to **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) intending to destroy or damage such property or being reckless as to whether such property would be destroyed or damaged and being reckless as to whether the life of a person would thereby be endangered
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(2), 1(3) and 4 of the Criminal Damage Act 1971.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
committed arson in that without lawful excuse
destroyed/damaged property by fire
intending to destroy/damage such property or
being reckless as to whether life would thereby be endangered

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
This CJS Code and Standard Offence Wording document OBSOLETE from 31/12/11. New version at CJS Code CD71003 and H8111.

(i) With aggravated offence, intent to endanger life must be charged separately; see R v Hoof (1981).
(ii) The consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required where damage to spouse's property (section 30(4) of the Theft Act 1968).
(iii) Property damaged/destroyed may belong to defendant.
(iv) The same incident may involve separate activities, some causing ordinary damage and some damage by fire (for example, protestors break into a laboratory building, smash laboratory equipment and set fire to some files). In such circumstances they are separate offences and best charged as such (R v Booth 1999).
